module_title: Basics of Space Technology and ISRO's Foundation
introduction: Space technology involves the use of satellites, space stations, and launch vehicles to explore space and improve life on Earth (weather forecasting, GPS, DTH TV). India's space journey is one of the most cost-effective and successful in the world.

core_concepts.title: Formation of ISRO
core_concepts.description:
The Indian Space Research Organisation (ISRO) was formed on **August 15, 1969**. It superseded INCOSPAR (set up in 1962). 
Headquarters: Bengaluru. 
Launch Center: Satish Dhawan Space Centre (SDSC), Sriharikota, Andhra Pradesh.

core_concepts.title: Father of the Indian Space Program
core_concepts.description: **Dr. Vikram Sarabhai** is universally recognized as the father of the Indian space program. He envisioned utilizing space technology for the benefit of the common man, not just for space exploration.

core_concepts.title: First Milestones
core_concepts.description:
1. **First Satellite (Aryabhata):** Launched in 1975. *Note: It was launched using a Soviet Union launch vehicle (Kosmos-3M), not an Indian one.* 
2. **First Indigenous Launch:** The 'Rohini' satellite (RS-1) was the first to be placed in orbit by an Indian-made launch vehicle, the **SLV-3**, in 1980 (Project Director: Dr. A.P.J. Abdul Kalam).

core_concepts.title: Basic Types of Orbits
core_concepts.description:
1. **Low Earth Orbit (LEO):** Very close to Earth (approx. 200 to 2,000 km altitude). Used for earth observation, spying, and the International Space Station (ISS). 
2. **Geostationary Orbit (GEO):** Very far from Earth (exactly **35,786 km** above the equator). Satellites here take 24 hours to orbit the Earth, so they appear 'stationary' from the ground. Used for DTH TV and communications.

important_entities.name: Dr. A.P.J. Abdul Kalam
important_entities.significance: Before becoming the 'Missile Man' and the President of India, Dr. Kalam led the development of India's first Satellite Launch Vehicle (SLV-3), giving India the capability to launch its own satellites.

trap_alerts_and_exceptions.explanation: Exam Trap: If the question asks, 'Which was India's first satellite?', the answer is **Aryabhata**. But if it asks, 'Which was the first satellite launched by an INDIAN launch vehicle?', the answer is **Rohini (RS-1)**.

mnemonics_and_tricks.memory_phrase: LEO is Low, GEO is Far
mnemonics_and_tricks.explanation: LEO (Low Earth Orbit) is just a few hundred kilometers up. GEO (Geostationary) is a massive 36,000 km up.

exam_strategy_tips: A guaranteed question in SSC/Railways: 'Where is the headquarters of ISRO located?' Answer: Bengaluru.
